headline: Hiring a Bathroom Addition Contractor: Mistakes to Avoid Before Signing
articleBody:
Adding a bathroom is a significant project that touches almost every trade in residential construction. Because so many mechanical systems intersect in a compact room, simple oversight can lead to expensive fixes down the road.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:

1. Starting work before pulling required permits. Adding plumbing lines, running new lighting circuits, or altering walls requires municipal permits. Beginning demolition without them risks stop-work orders and uninspected concealed work.

2. Venting exhaust fans into concealed spaces. Never vent bathroom moisture into an attic, soffit, or wall cavity. Exhaust systems must discharge directly outdoors to protect structural framing from damp air.

3. Underestimating plumbing line requirements. New toilets and showers demand correct pipe sizing, vent stacks, and drain slope. Tying into existing lines without checking capacity leads to drainage failure.

4. Selecting finishes before confirming rough-in clearances. Buying a vanity or shower enclosure before confirming valve positions and doorway swings often leads to costly returns or awkward layouts.

5. Skimping on wet-area waterproofing. Tile and grout alone do not stop water penetration. Skipping an approved waterproof membrane behind shower walls guarantees water damage to wall studs.

When Professional Guidance Helps:
Bringing in an experienced contractor ensures framing modifications, licensed trade coordination, and moisture management follow local standards from day one.
